{
  "subtype": "causal_attribution",
  "outcome_variable": "non_recommendation_outcome (Recommended = no)",
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "aircraft_product_mismatch",
      "causal_role": "treatment",
      "named_in_query": false,
      "rationale": "Captures whether the delivered product matched what was expected (downgrade, aircraft swap, older config instead of Qsuite). This is a candidate CAUSE of non-recommendation, not a common cause of another treatment and the outcome. It is a parallel driver, i.e. a treatment/explanatory factor, not a confounder."
    },
    {
      "name": "ground_service_quality",
      "causal_role": "treatment",
      "named_in_query": false,
      "rationale": "Check-in/lounge/baggage experience is a candidate cause whose effect on recommendation is being attributed. Not a common antecedent of another treatment and the outcome."
    },
    {
      "name": "food_beverage_quality",
      "causal_role": "treatment",
      "named_in_query": false,
      "rationale": "Service-quality dimension acting as a candidate cause of (non-)recommendation. A parallel driver, not a confounder."
    },
    {
      "name": "crew_service_consistency",
      "causal_role": "treatment",
      "named_in_query": false,
      "rationale": "Crew attentiveness is a candidate cause of the outcome. It does not cause the other service dimensions, so it is a competing treatment, not a confounder."
    },
    {
      "name": "seat_comfort_privacy",
      "causal_role": "treatment",
      "named_in_query": false,
      "rationale": "Seat/privacy experience is a direct candidate cause of recommendation. Parallel driver, not a common cause of another treatment and the outcome."
    },
    {
      "name": "ife_connectivity_issues",
      "causal_role": "treatment",
      "named_in_query": false,
      "rationale": "In-flight entertainment/wifi problems are a candidate cause of dissatisfaction/non-recommendation. Treatment, not confounder."
    },
    {
      "name": "pricing_value_mismatch",
      "causal_role": "treatment",
      "named_in_query": false,
      "rationale": "Perceived value-for-money is a candidate cause of the outcome. It is a driver, not a common cause of a treatment and the outcome."
    },
    {
      "name": "expectation_gap",
      "causal_role": "mediator",
      "named_in_query": false,
      "rationale": "The realised gap between expectation and experience sits ON the causal path between the service dimensions (treatments) and the recommendation outcome; it summarises the effect of the treatments rather than confounding it. Adjusting for it would be a mistake, so it cannot count as a confounder."
    },
    {
      "name": "expectation_versus_reality_gap",
      "causal_role": "mediator",
      "named_in_query": false,
      "rationale": "Duplicate of expectation_gap; a post-treatment mediator/near-restatement of the outcome, not a confounder."
    },
    {
      "name": "inflight_entertainment_and_connectivity",
      "causal_role": "treatment",
      "named_in_query": false,
      "rationale": "Duplicate of ife_connectivity_issues; a candidate cause / competing treatment, not a confounder."
    },
    {
      "name": "pricing_and_value_mismatch",
      "causal_role": "treatment",
      "named_in_query": false,
      "rationale": "Duplicate of pricing_value_mismatch; candidate cause of the outcome, not a confounder."
    },
    {
      "name": "seat_comfort_and_privacy",
      "causal_role": "treatment",
      "named_in_query": false,
      "rationale": "Duplicate of seat_comfort_privacy; parallel driver / treatment, not a confounder."
    }
  ],
  "treatment_present": true,
  "treatment_columns": [
    "aircraft_product_mismatch",
    "ground_service_quality",
    "food_beverage_quality",
    "crew_service_consistency",
    "seat_comfort_privacy",
    "ife_connectivity_issues",
    "pricing_value_mismatch",
    "inflight_entertainment_and_connectivity",
    "pricing_and_value_mismatch",
    "seat_comfort_and_privacy"
  ],
  "confounders": [],
  "confounder_quality": 0.0,
  "rationale": "The operator produced a broad, largely duplicated set of parallel service-quality dimensions (aircraft/product, ground service, food, crew, seat, IFE, pricing) plus two expectation-gap columns. Every service dimension is a CANDIDATE CAUSE (treatment) whose effect on non-recommendation is being attributed, and the expectation-gap columns are post-treatment MEDIATORS that lie on the causal path from those drivers to the outcome. Crucially, NONE of the columns is a confounder in the required sense: a variable that plausibly causes BOTH a treatment and the outcome and that must be adjusted for to avoid bias. No structural common causes (e.g., route/sector, aircraft-assignment policy, traveller type, reviewer expectations set before the flight, or seasonality) were surfaced as separate adjustment variables — those that exist (Route, Type of Traveller) are already in the original table and were not among the added columns. So while a treatment is present (indeed many competing treatments), the confounder-control component of the causal-attribution claim is entirely unmet, and one of the added constructs (expectation gap) is a mediator that would bias the estimate if 'adjusted for.' This is a driver/decomposition set rather than a genuine causal-estimation design; the technical claim FAILS on confounders."
}
